hoover.summaryNote: Hoover is the second-ranked team in the league and the deepest lineup top-to-bottom. Every spot in the order is a threat — there are no easy outs. They score in bunches: expect multi-run innings and pressure on every pitch. Their lone loss was to undefeated St. Catherines.

lineup.tip: Elite table-setter. 17-for-19 on the season — the best pure hitter in the league. Gets on base at will and scores in nearly every game. 1 HR and high ISO — OF plays deep.
lineup.pitchTip: Keep it low — his power numbers demand you avoid belt-high pitches. No meatballs.

lineup.tip: Consistent run-producer with 12 runs scored. Has gap power and hit a solo HR vs St. Catherines. His extra-base hits suggest balls getting into the gaps — OF plays deep and shades the alleys.
lineup.pitchTip: Has home run power — keep it low and off the fat part of the plate.

lineup.pitchTip: 5 doubles this season — don't give him anything easy to drive. Keep pitches low to limit extra-base damage.

franklin.summaryNote: The Franklin Falcons are a high-variance offense that can explode for 20-plus runs — they dropped 22 on Washington in a 22-21 thriller and hung 20 on Carey in a blowout — but they have also been shellacked by 16 runs twice, so they are not a machine, they are a mood. Todd Lanam leads the league in doubles with 8 in just 4 games, and the middle of the order produces at a rate that makes any one-run deficit feel recoverable in an instant. Opponents must treat every inning as a potential crooked-number situation; there is no safe lead against this lineup when it is clicking.

st-catherines.summaryNote: St. Catherines enter this game as the only undefeated team in the league, having run through a gauntlet that includes a dramatic 22-21 takedown of Hoover — a team that had been considered among the league's elite. They score nearly 19 runs per game and hit as a collective monster, with no clear weak spot in a rotation that has sent as many as 17 different players to the plate across five weeks. Their depth is their defining edge: even role players carry dangerous averages, and the lineup rarely gives pitchers a breather from top to bottom.

lincoln-lions.summaryNote: The Lincoln Lions are a disciplined, contact-heavy lineup that punished a weak Franklin squad 20-11 but have struggled against elite competition, getting outscored 32-8 in blowout losses to St. Catherines and Hoover. At 3-2-1 they remain a legitimate mid-tier threat: they spread hits across the full lineup, post a .471 team average, and rarely go cold as a unit. Their Achilles heel is a lack of true power — just one HR and a modest .596 team SLG — meaning they depend on stringing together contact and manufacturing runs.
lincoln-lions.lineupNote: The Lions dress a full 12-13 players every game, with consistent contributions from top to bottom; no single ace bat, but almost no automatic outs either. Their rotation is deep enough that pulling one hitter rarely changes the calculus.

washington-wildkittens.summaryNote: The Washington Wildkittens are a dangerous .500 club whose 3-3 record dramatically undersells their offensive firepower — three of their losses came by a single run, including a gut-punch 21-22 defeat to Franklin and a 14-15 heartbreaker against Hoover. Geheran leads the charge with a team-best 17 hits and 15 RBI across six games, anchoring a balanced lineup that scores 13+ runs per game. Despite carrying zero home runs, the Wildkittens punish gaps with 14 doubles and generate runs in volume through a relentless contact attack and clutch RBI production from multiple bats.
washington-wildkittens.lineupNote: Washington rotates 13+ players with near-universal depth — ten players have logged three or more games, and the bottom third of the order can still hurt you with run-scoring contact. Expect regular rotation at all spots; no clear weak link in the batting order.

lineup.tip: Team's offensive engine — 17 hits, 15 RBI in 6 games (.739 AVG, 0.88 RBI/H). ISO .217 with 3D/1T. 9-for-12 last 3 games and not cooling off.

Do not let their record lull you into complacency — they can put up a crooked number in a hurry.

roosevelt-blue.summaryNote: Roosevelt Blue is a 2-3 rebuilding squad that has shown genuine offensive punch in bursts -- their 18-6 demolition of Carey in week 4 demonstrated what this lineup can do when everything clicks, but a 15-3 blowout loss to St. Catherines the following week exposed their inconsistency. Three separate players have gone yard (Shapiro, Ortega, Ding), meaning power is distributed rather than concentrated, and they closed the most recent week by beating Washington Wildkittens 9-6 to take 2 of their last 3. At a .491 team average they make contact, but a .621 slugging mark tells you most of that contact is singles -- gaps and extra bases will come from a handful of specific threats worth knowing by name.

carey.summaryNote: Carey sits at 1-4 but their record undersells a roster loaded with contact hitters — they nearly upset Washington in week 1, losing by a single run 14-13, and their lone win came against Burlingame-Expansion 10-7. Several players carry alarming ISO in limited samples: O'Hare posts a 1.000 ISO (1 HR, 2 triples in just 7 AB) and Batenchuch sits at .600 ISO from 3 doubles in only 5 AB, making the bottom of their lineup potentially the most dangerous part. Their blowout losses to Franklin (20-8) and Roosevelt-Blue (18-6) suggest inconsistency rather than outright weakness, and a deep rotating roster means fresh bats can appear in any game.

gamePlan.heading: Neutralize Wright early — he is scorching hot.
gamePlan.tip: 9-for-10 last 3 games, .786 AVG, 1 HR — pitch low and away, no belt-high fastballs. Getting him out first AB sets the tone.

gamePlan.heading: Treat Corde as a cleanup hitter if he is in the lineup.
gamePlan.tip: 5 RBI, 1 HR, 1.333 ISO in one game — pitch away, never elevated. Consider pitching around him in high-leverage spots with runners on.

gamePlan.heading: Do not underestimate them based on the 1-3-1 record.
gamePlan.tip: Lost to Washington by 1 run (week 4) and tied Lincoln 14-14 (week 7) — two of four non-wins decided by a run or a tie. Do not underestimate.

gamePlan.heading: Shade the outfield to the gaps against Whittier and Anguera.
gamePlan.tip: Whittier (.333 ISO, triple) and Anguera (triple) can drive balls into the alleys — play OF slightly deeper and toward the gaps for both.

gamePlan.heading: Keep Williams and Conti off base — they are your table-setter problem.
gamePlan.tip: Williams (+4 R_diff) and Conti (+3 R_diff) start rallies at the top. Retire them quickly so Dabrik, Rodriguez, and Johnston face empty bases.
